column1: # Smoke-matrix expectation table (phase-15 §B). Checked into the repo so a capability regression shows
# up as a diff here. Each row boots example-golden-path once with the given kill-switch toggles and
# asserts: /actuator/health is UP, every capability in PRESENT appears in /actuator/platform, and none
# in ABSENT does. Columns are TAB-separated: id, jvm_args, present, absent.
# jvm_args: space-separated -D flags applied to the boot ("-" for none).
# present/absent: comma-separated capability names as they appear in /actuator/platform (note data-jpa).
# Security is never toggled off (it stays on in every row, per the spec) and the script additionally
# asserts an unauthenticated business call is rejected in the baseline row. Capabilities the reference
# service STRUCTURALLY depends on — messaging (EventPublisher), data-jpa (OrderRepository), resilience
# (RetryableOperation) — are not toggled off, because the app cannot boot without those beans; the
# matrix instead pins their presence and toggles the capabilities that degrade to no-ops (cache, audit).
# Capabilities the service never wires (flags, storage, locking, ratelimit) are pinned ABSENT so a
# stray dependency that dragged one in would fail the matrix.
# id
baseline
cache-off
audit-off
cache-and-audit-off
security-mode-pinned
no-extra-capabilities
